> **Coverage rule.** Every material item in the plan and the execution record must end up in exactly one of three places: represented below, folded into a section it materially belongs to, or recorded as an explicit Omit with a reason in the companion Fidelity Ledger (`HUMAN-FIDELITY-LEDGER-TEMPLATE.md`, never published). Silence is not a valid treatment for anything material. Any item classified Preserve must be quoted verbatim in the Ledger, not paraphrased.
> **Known limit**: the plan's Implementation Constraints table has no ID column in the source, so the automatic coverage check cannot verify that section mechanically — treat it with the same care manually.
>
> Source: a locked build plan and its matching completed execution record — the two are always the same version pair. Do not run this against a plan or execution record that is still in draft.

# [Work Item Title] — Delivery Summary

**Status: [Delivered / Partially delivered / Not yet delivered]**

> One line, directly under the title, using the exact same three words as the Status section below — never a looser paraphrase. This lets a reader get the bottom line before reading anything else.

> Source: the plan's own closing summary (its Director's Summary section) + the execution record's closing summary (its own Director's Summary section) — the overview portions only. Class: Preserve, merged rather than rewritten from nothing (both sources are already written to be human-readable).
> A reader who stops after this paragraph should understand what was asked for and what happened. State the outcome using the same three-word status vocabulary as the badge above and the Status section below — this paragraph and that section must never tell a reader two different things.

## Status

> Source: the execution record's own verification results, its completion self-report, and the plan-owner's independent post-build review verdict — two different people's assessments, not one. Class: Preserve — this is the direct answer to "is this actually done," it must not be hedged or blurred.
>
> **Reconciliation rule, required whenever the two disagree**: if the plan-owner's independent post-build verdict exists, it wins over the builder's own self-report — it is the independent check, the self-report is not. Map it as follows:
> - Independent verdict says ready to finalize → **Delivered**.
> - Independent verdict says needs more work or revision required → **Not yet delivered**.
> - Independent verdict says complete but flags a risk or caveat → **Partially delivered**.
> - Independent verdict falls outside these three (an "other" case with free-text explanation) → read the explanation and choose the closest fit; do not default silently.
>
> If the independent post-build review has not happened yet, fall back to the builder's own self-report — but the Fidelity Ledger must record that this is an unreviewed self-report, not an independently checked status. That distinction must never be silently dropped.

Collapse the status into exactly one of three states — pick one, do not invent a fourth:

- [ ] **Delivered** — done and verified against the acceptance criteria below.
- [ ] **Partially delivered** — some but not all acceptance criteria met, or delivered with a flagged caveat; state which.
- [ ] **Not yet delivered** — blocked or still pending review; state why.

> Source: the plan's build objective and task breakdown ("the ask"), plus its acceptance criteria ("how success was checked"). Class: Preserve.
> Write these as two clearly distinct parts. The ask is what was requested, in one or two sentences. The checks are only the conditions a reader could use to verify it — do not restate the ask a second time in slightly different words. ## Open Items

> Source: deviations from the plan, issues encountered during the work, and known limitations — three different questions, grouped here so a reader who wants "what isn't perfect" reads one section instead of three, and a reader who wants none of it can skip one heading. Give each part its own short subheading; do not blur them into one paragraph.
> If a limitation or issue is the same fact already stated in the Status section above, do not repeat it at length here — a one-line cross-reference is enough. Reserve full detail for whichever section is the more natural home.

### Deviation From the Plan

> Class: Preserve — substance must not be softened. If the source has a deviation, the reader must be able to tell it actually happened and what it changed.
> If none, write exactly:

> No material deviation from the plan.

[...]

### Issues Encountered

> Class: Compress, but any issue significant enough to affect the outcome or the reader's confidence stays in, even if that makes this part longer.

### Known Limitation

> Class: Preserve — risk-relevant, must survive compression intact.

## Feedback From Testing

> Source: the recorded report from the person who actually tried the finished work, any small requests raised at the same time, and — this is the part draft v1 silently dropped — **whether each item was actually resolved**. Class: Preserve for the findings and requests themselves (do not paraphrase away specifics, soften severity, or drop an item because it is minor); Preserve for resolution status too — a reader must be able to tell what was flagged AND what happened to it, not just the first half.
